_doc: STATELESS for now — internal tool, voice is not a critical surface. DealFindrs runs its own bespoke voice stack (/api/voice/bind-session, /api/voice/chat, /api/voice/elevenlabs-connect, /api/webhooks/elevenlabs, a voice_sessions table, and 5 separate agents: ASSESSMENT/BASICS/DERISK/FINANCIAL/PROPERTY). It has no convai memory routes and no convai_memory/convai_agents tables, so the canonical mid-call round-trip the probe asserts has nothing behind it. Operator decision 2026-07-27: internal use, voice non-critical, classed stateless. Two conditions that would flip this: the tool becomes externally exposed, or voice becomes a primary rather than incidental surface. SEPARATE ISSUE, independent of this opt-out and worth closing on its own: src/lib/elevenlabs/webhook-verify.ts is a LOCAL FORK of the hub's signature verification — its own comments say it 'matches the algorithm in @caistech/elevenlabs-convai/src/webhook.ts'. That is a @caistech-first violation; consume verifyWebhookSignature from the package instead of maintaining a second copy of a security primitive.
